title: This Town Says Its Own Name Wrong on Purpose #history #shorts
description:
In 1889, settlers on Horse Creek, Wyoming, asked for a post office named Tibo, a Shoshone word for "stranger" and the Shoshone people's nickname for the Welsh missionary John Roberts. The form came back amended in red ink: Dubois, after Fred Dubois of Idaho. Who made the change is disputed, and the story that locals say "DOO-boys" to spite him is local legend.

The scenes are an animated dramatization.

#history #shorts #weirdhistory
comment: So what do you think: should Dubois change its name back to Tibo?
